claim: From the device card's gate-stack geometry alone (before any measurement), the D=0 line's density window was predicted to reach much higher magnitude on the electron side (~+3.5e12 cm^-2) than the hole side (~-1.0e12 cm^-2) given the gate-voltage limits, so the investigation was expected to end up electron-side-biased unless the charge-neutrality point sat well off zero gate voltage.
context: Stated in a pre-measurement state summary while waiting on the autonomy grant, before gate C or any sweep had been run; a pure forward calculation from the geometry prior, not yet checked against data.
evidence: Forward computation from device-card gate-stack thicknesses/lever-arm prior; no sweep data cited.

claim: Ran a four-leg gate-current-sanity-check liveness sweep (each gate 0 to its card limit, other gate parked at 0, field and Si gate at 0) at 101 points/leg, 1 s delay, integration set for ~2.2 s/pt, lock-in sensitivity 500 microV, with a 1 nA gate-current auto-abort guard, priced at ~20 minutes total.
context: First sweep of the cooldown; chosen as the liveness/gross-safety branch of the stacking investigation recipe before any gatemap, since there were no prior references for this device this session.
evidence: Sweep parameters stated in the landed rationale cell; four run directories produced.

claim: The device passed current on the provided source-drain contacts (drain current about 9.86-9.94 nA of the 10 nA bias) and the wired voltage-probe pair read a resistance spanning roughly 60-330 ohms across all four gate-sweep legs at zero field.
context: Read from the four gate-current-sanity-check legs after they completed, used to certify basic device liveness before proceeding to the gatemap.
evidence: Per-leg drain current and Rxx ranges computed from the four run TSVs.

claim: Each gate's 1D liveness sweep showed two resistance maxima (top gate near -0.21 V and +0.11 V; back gate near -0.26 V and +0.14 V), with a position ratio between the two gates matching the geometry-prior capacitance ratio; interpreted as two charge-neutrality points in series between the voltage probes, i.e. two regions of different intrinsic doping (offset roughly 0.6e12 cm^-2 by the geometry prior), with weak resistance contrast over the metallic floor. Whether these are two separate flake domains or a contact-adjacent artifact was left open pending the gatemap.
context: Read immediately after the four gate-current-sanity-check legs completed, comparing the peak positions and ratios seen through each gate.
evidence: Peak voltage/resistance values read off each leg's R(V) trace; ratio of peak positions compared to the geometry-prior capacitance ratio.

claim: Designed the first zero-field gatemap over the full top-gate range at 20 mV steps (66 points) by the back-gate range from its negative limit up to +1.2 V (rather than its full +2.0 V positive limit) at 40 mV steps (63 rows), deliberately truncating back-gate coverage because the geometry prior predicted that region would be metallic and uninformative for the charge-neutrality line or the fan, saving roughly 35 minutes; sensitivity set to 20 microV, fast delay 1 s, slow delay 3 s, leak guard active.
context: Planned right after the gate-C liveness legs passed, to resolve whether the two resistance maxima seen in 1D were parallel ridges (two domains) and to calibrate the gate-to-density conversion.
evidence: Window and step sizes stated in the landed rationale cell, with the back-gate truncation justified from the geometry prior's predicted charge-neutrality-line trajectory.

claim: Aborted the first gatemap attempt after its opening rows because the lock-in railed (about 2.2 kilohms against a 2 kilohm full-scale) along the charge-neutrality ridge at large displacement field, then re-ran the identical map at a five-times-larger full-scale (100 microV instead of 20 microV), explicitly trading away low-resistance readout resolution to avoid saturating the higher-resistance ridge region.
context: Triggered by the first-rows checkpoint on the initial gatemap sweep; the abort and resize happened before most of the map had been collected, at a cost of about 3 minutes of instrument time.
evidence: Railed value (~2.18 kilohms, full-scale fraction 1.09) reported from the aborted run's first two rows; re-run parameters stated in the follow-up rationale cell.

claim: The completed gatemap resolved the earlier ambiguity: it shows one dominant charge-neutrality ridge running diagonally across the map plus a fainter, parallel ridge offset about 0.19 V lower in top-gate voltage (identified as the second peak seen in the earlier 1D liveness legs) — i.e. two parallel ridges consistent with two distinct regions of the flake in series, rather than a single contact-adjacent artifact.
context: Read from the full 2D gatemap once it completed, directly following up on the two-maxima ambiguity flagged from the 1D liveness legs.
evidence: Ridge positions and slopes fit from the 2D resistance map; ridge separation (~0.19 V in top-gate voltage) reported.

claim: The dominant charge-neutrality ridge's resistance grows from about 240 ohms near zero displacement field to about 2.4 kilohms (saturating) at a raw displacement field of about +0.25 V/nm, indicating a displacement-field-tunable gap at the charge-neutrality point; explicitly flagged as not itself diagnostic of stacking order, since more than one candidate stacking could produce such a gap.
context: Read from the completed gatemap's resistance-vs-displacement-field trace along the dominant ridge.
evidence: Ridge resistance values at raw D~0 and at raw D~+0.25 V/nm from the 2D map.

claim: Fitting the dominant ridge's slope in the gatemap's operating window gives a data-calibrated back-gate/top-gate capacitance ratio of 0.773, about 11% below the geometry-prior value (~0.864); this discrepancy was judged to most likely reflect an hBN-thickness error in the prior rather than a wiring/contact-role transposition.
context: Derived immediately after the gatemap completed, used to set the session's gate-to-density (n, D) calibration for all subsequent measurements.
evidence: Linear fit of ridge position (top-gate vs back-gate) over the low-|D| operating window, rms of the fit residual reported; compared against the geometry-prior capacitance ratio.

claim: The physical zero of displacement field was located from the symmetry vertex of the dominant ridge's resistance minimum plotted against raw displacement field (vertex at roughly +0.012-0.013 V/nm raw), and this offset was adopted as the D=0 reference for all subsequent gate-voltage-to-(n,D) conversions.
context: Computed as part of the post-gatemap calibration, using the ridge-resistance-vs-D curve's minimum as the physical marker for zero field.
evidence: Parabolic fit vertex of ridge resistance vs raw displacement field.

claim: The fainter, secondary region is electron-doped by about +0.43e12 cm^-2 relative to the dominant region; carried forward as a series-mosaic confound for the stacking read, on the reasoning that if it shares the same stacking template its Landau-level tones would sit at roughly 13% higher frequency than the dominant region's, likely overlapping the dominant region's tones at low relative weight rather than appearing as a separately resolvable set.
context: Derived from the fitted density offset between the two parallel gatemap ridges, used later to argue that the secondary region would not corrupt the main stacking call even if unresolved on its own.
evidence: Density offset between the two fitted ridge positions in the 2D gatemap.

claim: Designed and ran an SdH spot check on the electron side at a fixed density of +3.2e12 cm^-2 (D=0), sweeping field from 0 to 10 T (50 mT steps to 1 T, then 10 mT steps above, 921 points total), lock-in sensitivity fixed at 50 microV, delay set to zero (relying only on the magnet driver's built-in settle), priced at about 2 h 15 m; deliberately left the gates parked at the spot and field at 10 T at the end so the hole-side check could ride the magnet back down without re-traversing the range.
context: First density-resolved SdH measurement of the session, chosen at the high-density end of the electron side reachable at D=0 under the freshly derived gate calibration, to feed the tetralayer stacking Fermi-surface-count investigation.
evidence: Field grid, sensitivity, and point count stated in the landed rationale cell; spot density and target gate voltages computed from the run-5 calibration.

claim: The wired voltage-probe pair's raw resistance drops sharply (from about 52 to 12 ohms) within the first 0.5 T of field; interpreted as a Hall-voltage (rho_xy) admixture from the pair straddling a corner of the flake rather than being a clean longitudinal probe pair, judged harmless for extracting SdH oscillation frequencies but relevant to any quantitative use of the raw resistance as rho_xx.
context: Noticed in the raw field trace of the electron-side spot check, before any FFT analysis was performed on the same run.
evidence: Raw R(B) trace of the electron-side spot check showing the sharp initial drop.

claim: The electron-side spot check's raw resistance trace shows deep oscillation minima near 4.25, 6.0, and 7.2 T (plus a shallower one near 4.95 T), consistent with a single 1/B-periodic pattern of period corresponding to a combined frequency around 29.3 T, alongside a full quantum-Hall plateau regime setting in above about 7.5 T.
context: Raw-data reading of the electron-side spot check before FFT analysis, used to motivate the subsequent frequency decomposition.
evidence: Minima positions and inferred filling factors read directly off the raw R(B) trace.

claim: FFT of the electron-side spot check resolves two dominant tones at about 7.3 T and 22.0 T that sum to about 29.3 T, matching the fourfold-degenerate total Landau-level frequency expected at this density once the geometry-prior density scale is rescaled by a factor of 0.886; the two tones partition the total roughly 0.25/0.75, close to the Bernal (ABAB) stacking model's predicted 0.23/0.77 partition at this density, with a weaker 14.7 T tone attributed to the second harmonic of the lighter tone. Provisional call: consistent with ABAB stacking, not yet strong pending further density- and temperature-dependent tests.
context: Main frequency-domain analysis of the electron-side spot check, the first density point analyzed toward the campaign's stacking-determination goal.
evidence: FFT peak frequencies and relative amplitudes over a 1-5.5 T window; comparison of the resolved partition ratio to the ABAB forward-model prediction at the same density.

claim: Designed and ran a second SdH spot check on the hole side, at the most negative density reachable on the D=0 line within the gate limits (about -1.2e12 cm^-2), riding the magnet down from 10 T to 0.3 T at 20 mT steps (486 points), sensitivity 50 microV; explicitly framed as a cheap, non-decisive preview rather than a decisive test, since a null result there would be resolution- and mass-limited rather than genuine evidence against the alternative stacking.
context: Chosen to sample both electron and hole sides with no prior expectation of which would be more informative, taking advantage of the electron-side check already having parked the magnet at 10 T.
evidence: Field grid and framing stated in the landed rationale cell; spot density set by the TG gate-voltage limit on the hole side of the D=0 line.

claim: The hole-side spot check shows broad, non-sinusoidal low-field features giving way to a fully symmetry-broken integer quantum-Hall ladder above about 5 T; its FFT content sits at and below the expected total frequency at this density (about 11.0 T), with candidate component frequencies near 4.4 T and 6.8 T that would sum close to that total (matching the ABAB near-charge-neutrality-point "semimetal" template), but the record could not cleanly separate the two component tones. Weighted as consistent with ABAB stacking but uninformative against the alternative (ABCA) stacking, since the alternative's predicted heavy-mass pocket would not be resolvable at this measurement's electron temperature regardless of which stacking is actually present.
context: Analysis of the completed hole-side spot check, run after the electron-side call had already suggested ABAB provisionally.
evidence: FFT peak positions and amplitudes over a 1-5 T window; comparison to the expected total frequency and to the ABAB near-neutrality forward-model prediction.

claim: The spacing of the integer quantum-Hall ladder minima above 4.5 T in the hole-side spot check gives an independently derived density scale of roughly 0.80-0.92 relative to the geometry-prior calibration, bracketing the 0.886 scale independently obtained from the electron-side Luttinger-sum analysis.
context: A lever-arm cross-check computed from the same hole-side run used for the stacking read, comparing two independent methods of pinning the absolute density scale.
evidence: Median 1/B spacing of quantum-Hall minima above 4.5 T converted to a density via the filling-factor relation, compared to the calibrated density at that gate point.

claim: Designed and ran a Landau fan on the electron side at D=0: density swept from about 1.60 to 3.25e12 cm^-2 (61 points) at each of 101 field rows spaced uniformly in 1/B from 1 to 10 T, sensitivity fixed at 100 microV, fast-axis delay 1.2 s, priced at about 3 h 55 m; the lower field bound (1.0 T) and lower density bound (~1.6e12) were both set from the electron-side spot check's observed tone-onset behavior.
context: The main density-resolved measurement of the campaign, designed immediately after the electron- and hole-side spot checks to test whether the two candidate SdH branches track the ABAB model's predicted frequency-vs-density curves.
evidence: Fast/slow axis ranges, point counts, and sensitivity stated in the landed rationale cell; bounds justified from the electron-side spot check's tone-onset fields.

claim: The completed Landau fan shows clean Landau-level rays across the whole density-field window from 1 T upward, with no missing or leakage-truncated points (all 6161 planned points collected) and a quantum-Hall regime setting in above about 7.5 T.
context: Raw-data read of the fan once it finished, before the per-column frequency analysis.
evidence: Point-count check against the planned grid; visual/qualitative description of the raw 2D resistance map.

claim: Tracking two SdH branches column-by-column across the fan's 61 densities shows both following the ABAB-stacking model's predicted frequency-vs-density curves under the single 0.886 density scale (light branch spanning roughly 3.0-7.5 T against a model curve of 1.8-6.3 T; heavy branch spanning roughly 13.9-22.1 T against a model curve of 13-22.9 T), while an alternative trilayer (monolayer+bilayer) stacking model was excluded because its predicted partner-branch trajectory (near 1-2 T) did not match either observed branch.
context: Per-column FFT analysis of the completed Landau fan, the campaign's primary density-dependence test of the stacking hypothesis.
evidence: Per-column FFT peak tracks over the fan's 61 density columns, overlaid against ABAB and trilayer forward-model curves at the same (rescaled) densities.

claim: A third tracked tone equals the sum of the light and heavy branch frequencies at essentially every fan column (the total matching the expected fourfold-degenerate frequency across the whole density range), while a fourth, nearly density-independent tone equals their difference at every column; the flat, non-Onsager trajectory of this difference tone was read as establishing that the sum tone is a combination/intermodulation orbit of the two real Fermi pockets (allowed by symmetry under ABAB stacking) rather than a separate pocket belonging to an alternative (ABCA) stacking domain.
context: Central discrimination step of the campaign: distinguishing whether the tone at the total expected frequency is a genuine third pocket (which would argue for a different, ABCA, stacking) or a combination tone of the other two (consistent with ABAB).
evidence: Per-column tracking of the sum and difference tones across all 61 fan columns, noting the difference tone's flat density trajectory versus the sum and branch tones' density-dependent trajectories.

claim: No supra-linear, Dirac-like third branch (the signature expected under an alternative ABCB stacking) was seen anywhere in the fan, but this exclusion was flagged as weak at low density, since such a branch's predicted amplitude there would fall below the fan's frequency-resolution floor regardless of whether it were actually present.
context: One of several forward-model comparisons run against the completed fan data as part of the mandatory verification checklist for the stacking call.
evidence: Absence of a matching feature in the per-column FFT tracks, compared against the ABCB forward-model's predicted low-density branch amplitude and the fan's frequency resolution.

claim: The fourfold-degeneracy density scale (0.886) extracted from the electron-side fan/spot-check data is consistent with the independent scale (0.80-0.92) obtained from the hole-side integer-quantum-Hall ladder spacing, taken together as evidence of no spin/valley (flavor) polarization at this gate/field operating point.
context: A degeneracy cross-check run as part of the mandatory verification checklist, comparing two independently derived absolute density scales from opposite carrier sides.
evidence: Comparison of the 0.886 scale (electron-side Luttinger sum and fan) against the 0.80-0.92 scale (hole-side quantum-Hall ladder spacing).

claim: Designed and ran a Lifshitz-Kosevich mass-ladder measurement at the same electron-side spot (density +3.2e12 cm^-2, D=0): six temperature rungs (base ~1.2 K plus 6, 10, 15, 22, and 30 K, set via the heater's authorized dual-loop method with a hover-acceptance criterion), field swept back and forth over a fixed 2-7 T window at 25 mT per rung, sensitivity 50 microV, priced at about 5 h 10 m; explicitly decided that because the rig's nominal base electron temperature (per the rig card) is expected to exceed the thermometer reading, the mass fits would rely on the heated rungs and treat the base-temperature point only as a free cross-check rather than a fit input.
context: Final data-taking step of the campaign, designed to separate the two SdH branches by their effective mass and to determine whether the combined-frequency tone's mass is consistent with a combination orbit rather than a separate pocket.
evidence: Rung temperatures, field window, and heating/hover method stated in the landed rationale cell; the base-rung treatment justified by the rig card's stated typical base electron temperature versus the live thermometer reading.

claim: Fitting the lightest SdH tone's amplitude versus temperature over the heated ladder rungs gives an effective mass of 0.028 +/- 0.002 (free-electron-mass units), matching the ABAB-stacking model's predicted light-pocket mass at this density essentially exactly.
context: Primary Lifshitz-Kosevich mass extraction from the completed six-rung temperature ladder, used as one of the campaign's decisive stacking-discrimination checks.
evidence: Lifshitz-Kosevich curve fit of the light tone's FFT amplitude across the five heated rungs, with fit uncertainty; compared to the ABAB forward-model's predicted mass at the same density.

claim: The heavier SdH tone's fitted mass is dependent on which part of the field window is used for the fit (about 0.038 in the lower half of the window versus about 0.057 in the upper half, 0.041 over the full window), reported as an unresolved fork rather than a single value; the resulting light-to-heavy mass ratio (1.4-2.0) falls short of the ABAB model's predicted ratio of about 2.2 at this density.
context: Second half of the Lifshitz-Kosevich mass extraction, needed to test the ABAB model's predicted mass ratio between the two branches.
evidence: Lifshitz-Kosevich fits of the heavy tone's amplitude performed separately over the full field window and over its lower and upper halves, compared to the ABAB model's predicted heavy mass and mass ratio.

claim: The mass fitted for the combined (sum-frequency) tone (0.051-0.069) is heavier than the heavy branch and, in the upper field window, approaches the sum of the light and heavy branch masses; because this is heavier than the light branch alone, a simple "beat" interpretation (two closely spaced frequencies from a single pocket, rather than two separate pockets) was excluded, read as a decisive indicator of two genuinely distinct Fermi pockets plus a combination orbit rather than a separate third pocket.
context: Final step of the mandatory verification checklist tying the mass-ladder results back to the fan's tone-origin question (combination orbit versus separate ABCA pocket).
evidence: Lifshitz-Kosevich fit of the sum-frequency tone's mass compared to the sum of the independently fitted light and heavy branch masses, and to the light branch mass alone.

claim: The unheated base-temperature rung's tone amplitudes fall on or near the mass-fit curves extrapolated from the heated rungs, implying an effective electron temperature at base of roughly 4 K or below at this operating point -- colder than the rig card's stated typical base electron temperature of about 8 K.
context: A consistency check on the base rung, run after the heated-rung mass fits were obtained, to see whether the excluded base point was itself consistent with those fits.
evidence: Comparison of the base rung's per-tone FFT amplitudes to the Lifshitz-Kosevich curves fit from the five heated rungs.

claim: Final campaign call for the device's wired voltage-probe pair (which probes the two series-connected doping regions together): the stacking is ABAB (Bernal), rated "strong" -- based on the closing Luttinger frequency sum, both SdH branches tracking the ABAB model's density dependence across the fan, the combination-tone origin of the summed frequency, and the Lifshitz-Kosevich mass split (light mass matching the model exactly, with a decisive beat exclusion) -- with explicit hedges that the heavy-branch mass remains an unresolved extraction-window fork and that only a single voltage-probe pair was available, so a different stacking confined to the weakly-doped secondary region cannot be excluded.
context: Delivered as the campaign's final determination after all planned measurements (gate C, gatemap, both spot checks, fan, and temperature ladder) were complete, citing the full chain of evidence gathered across the session.
evidence: Cited evidence chain: run 6 Luttinger-sum partition and scale; run 8 fan branch-tracking, sum/difference tone behavior, and adjacent-stacking exclusion; runs 9-14 Lifshitz-Kosevich mass fits and beat exclusion; run 7 hole-side consistency and independent density-scale cross-check.

claim: The fainter, more lightly doped secondary region (probed only in series with the dominant region through the same voltage-probe pair) was judged uninformative on its own for the stacking call, since no tone set attributable solely to it was resolved -- its predicted tones (shifted to somewhat higher frequency than the dominant region's) were judged to fall within the frequency resolution of the dominant region's tones at low relative weight.
context: Delivered as part of the same final campaign call, addressing the series-mosaic confound identified back at the gatemap stage.
evidence: Absence of a separately resolvable tone set near the frequency shift (~13% higher) expected for the secondary region's density offset, across the fan and spot-check FFTs.

claim: Based on the ABAB stacking call, recommended deprioritizing further correlated/flat-band-physics investigation of this device, redirecting future campaign value toward conventional quantum-Hall degeneracy-lifting physics instead, noting the device already showed full quantum-Hall symmetry breaking by 5 T at low density on the hole side.
context: Closing recommendation appended immediately after the final stacking call, intended to guide any future session's choice of what to measure next on this device.
evidence: Cited the hole-side spot check's fully symmetry-broken integer ladder above ~5 T as the basis for judging the remaining physics value.

claim: At session close-out, explicitly ramped the magnet back to its session-start field value (0 T) as a deliberate endpoint choice, rather than leaving it at the temperature ladder's ending field, treating the field return as distinct from the state-restore used for gates and heaters.
context: Final action of the session, after the stacking call had been delivered, restoring the device to its initial condition for handoff.
evidence: Close-out rationale cell stating the field endpoint as an explicit decision separate from the captured bring-up state used to restore gates/heaters.
